turnout.txNote: About 10.6 million Texans vote, roughly 56% of registered voters: 7.74 million early plus about 2.9 million on Election Day. That's the highest midterm turnout on record, just short of 2024's 11.4 million.
turnout.dallas: Dallas County: about 830,000 votes, with Talarico near 68% (D+37), up from Harris's D+22 margin here in 2024.

factors.b: The generic congressional ballot averages D+8.9 (Silver Bulletin, Nov. 2), near its high for the cycle. Historically, a lead that size produces a comfortable House majority for the party ahead.

factors.t: Markets and forecasters agree on direction, not size
factors.b: Kalshi and Polymarket give Democrats about 75% for the Senate and 94% for the House. Decision Desk HQ is more cautious: 84% and 241 seats for the House. Our model averages them, which is why our House number lands between.

factors.t: Texas early vote broke the midterm record
factors.b: 7.74 million Texans voted early, 40.5% of registered voters, past 2018's record. Turnout jumped most in the big metros: Tarrant and Dallas counties are 12 to 14 points ahead of their 2022 pace.

factors.t: But the early electorate is not a Democratic landslide
factors.b: By primary history, 29.9% of early voters last voted in a Republican primary and 28.3% in a Democratic one; 39% have no primary history. Modeled estimates range from about R+8 (On Point) to roughly even (VoteHub's Tilt D for Talarico). Election Day voters are expected to lean Republican.

In the final On Point poll, Talarico led by 5.5 while Abbott led by 4.6. Among people who had already voted, Talarico led 54–44; among those who hadn't, it was 49–48. Abbott led Election Day voters by 12.

factors.t: Polls in Texas have missed toward Democrats before
factors.b: Texas polls have underestimated Republicans in several recent elections. We widen the Texas ranges for that, which is why a Paxton win is very much in play even though he trails.

flip.b: Election Day voters break about R+13 or more, enough to overcome the early-vote edge On Point estimates for Talarico, or the polls miss toward Republicans the way they did in 2020.
They hold Ohio, Maine and Texas and win both coin flips, Iowa and Kansas. That's roughly the 28% of simulations where Republicans finish with 50 or more seats.
The national environment tightens to about D+3 or less on the day, or Republicans sweep the toss-ups: about 9% of our simulations.
